newsitem.title: UK: Oil slips further, still looking shaky.
newsitem.headline: Oil slips further, still looking shaky.

text.p: Oil markets slipped a little lower on Monday and were looking shaky after shedding a sizeable chunk of their recent hefty gains.
London December futures for North Sea Brent blend closed down 22 cents at $22.25 a barrel after dumping $2.50 in two weeks from mid-October's six-year high.

Dealers said strength on the U.S. gasoline market was helping prop up a market threatening to test lower ground in the wake of last week's wholesale reversal of a four-month bull run, but weak heating oil was proving the stronger factor.
Gasoline is in relatively short supply in the United States because refineries have been maximising heating oil output to replenish low stocks ahead of winter.
Oil prices also got help from concerns over the imminent heart surgery planned for Russian leader Boris Yeltsin.
Political volatility at the centre of one of the world's biggest oil exporters could cause jitters in the oil market, dealers said.
Oil prices tumbled last week as investment funds took the view that prices were unlikely to stage a quick recovery to their recent post Gulf War highs.
Low heating oil stocks have underpinned oil prices since the summer amid concerns over possible shortages this winter.
But U.S. refinery heating oil output hit record levels last week and data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed a significant build in stocks.
